title: Push foam corner protectors onto all four corners of a framed picture before a move
instruction: Fit the four foam corner protectors onto the corners of the picture frame, then let go of them.
context: Movers and hand packers push snug foam corner and edge protectors onto framed pictures, mirrors, glass panels and furniture before wrapping them, so a knock in transit doesn't split a mitre or crack the glass (O*NET 53-7062, 53-7064: pad and protect goods for moving). Each protector grips by squeezing, so it must be lined up level with the edge and pushed fully home while the loose piece isn't shoved off its supports.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); the layout is the same in every trial. (1) Two padded blocks, fixed: pine 2x4 offcuts covered in grey carpet, 16 long (x), 8.9 wide and 3.8 tall, centred at x 30, y +18.5 and -18.5. (2) A picture frame lying face down on the blocks, 1.1 kg: oak moulding 3 wide and 2.5 thick, 30 front to back (x) by 40 across (y), centred at x 30, y 0; glass, mount and hardboard back fill its opening (from 4 mm behind its front to 5 mm short of its back). The blocks are under its two 30 cm sides, so each corner sticks out 7 past the blocks' ends. Its corners are at x 15 and 45, y +20 and -20. (3) Four white cross-linked polyethylene foam corner protectors, 20 g each: a block 7 x 7 and 4.5 tall with an L-shaped pocket cut into two adjacent sides, 4.5 deep each way and 2.55 tall, with 1 cm of foam above and below it. The pocket's open edges are bevelled 6 mm over their outer 10 mm, and its floor stands 2 mm proud until pressed (about 6 N at 1.5 mm). Each lies flat on the table (it is the same either way up) beside one corner, pocket facing it: the back of its pocket at the corner's x and 10 further out in y (y +30 or -30).
scoring: Judged at the end with a tape measure. A corner counts when a protector is fully on it and let go: the corner within 4 mm of the back of the pocket both ways; the pocket's floor under the frame's front and its roof over the frame's back, the foam squeezed onto the frame (no gap a 1 mm feeler gauge passes between the frame's front and the pocket floor); the protector square and level with the frame within 6 degrees; each gripper's fingertip centre at least 4 cm from the protector's middle. 0 if the frame was ever dropped (tilted over 15 degrees, or slid 1.5 cm down off a block) or doesn't end flat on both blocks (within 3 degrees). Otherwise 0.25 for each corner that counts, except that with all four counting it is 1.0 once the frame and all four protectors are still (each moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s), else 0.75. The trial ends at the run limit, or when 1.0 has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Pull the four protectors off and lay them back on their marks, pockets facing their corners; put the frame back centred on the blocks. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz control). The foam's squeeze is a sprung rigid floor in each pocket (4,000 N/m, 2 mm proud: about 6 N once on); the rest of the foam is rigid, and the bevels on the pocket's open edges stand in for foam giving at the opening. The frame is one rigid body: moulding plus one slab for the glass, mount and back. Foam and frame friction 0.6.
